scope: Batch review of E05-E09 only, from code and config in this repo (app/, config/, deploy/k8s, release/manifest.yaml, migrations). Not reviewed: all other items; the ERP MCP gateway, STS, payments API and Slack proxy implementations, which live outside this repo. Nothing was run. No challenges were run (separate process). Inventory: one MCP server (ERP, mcp_client.py), one in-process sub-agent (extractor.py), no peer-agent endpoint. Prescan hits H003/H004 (B11) and others owned by other batches were not resolved here.

findings.title: Verified, namespaced tools
findings.requirement: Identify each tool by a verified server identity plus the tool name. Base server identity on the verified endpoint, credential, or registry namespace. A server's self-reported name is neither unique nor trustworthy. Flag lookalike and duplicate names across servers. Test that a new server can't quietly swap its tool in for an approved one.

not_covered.problem: Hidden instructions inside a tool's metadata
A tool's description or schema changing after it was approved
Peer agent identity not authenticated on each message
Gateway not authenticating callers or authorizing each action

evidence.note: ERP tools are keyed by bare tool name; no verified server identity (endpoint/credential/namespace) in the key. Only one server is configured, but nothing prevents a later server or refresh from overwriting an entry.

checks.check: Tools are keyed by verified server identity (endpoint, credential, or registry namespace) plus tool name, never by bare tool name or a server's self-reported name.
checks.verify: 1) Find the tool registry or lookup map. 2) Check its key is a verified endpoint, credential, or registry namespace plus tool name. 3) Answer no if tools are keyed by bare tool name or the server's self-reported name (`serverInfo.name`), or a later server overwrites an earlier entry with the same tool name.
checks.quote: self._tools = {t["name"]: t for t in tools}
checks.note: ERP tools are keyed by bare tool name; no verified server identity (endpoint/credential/namespace) in the key. Only one server is configured, but nothing prevents a later server or refresh from overwriting an entry.

checks.check: The registry flags duplicate and lookalike tool names across servers.
checks.verify: 1) Trace name comparison across servers. 2) Construct repeated confusable substitutions, multiple edits and normalization-boundary examples, starting from an existing tool name; record canonical outputs, comparison result and registration outcome. 3) Answer no if a duplicate or demonstrated lookalike is accepted without a conflict flag. The existence of normalization/edit-distance code is insufficient; namespacing and approval binding do not satisfy this separate check.
checks.note: Duplicate names across tool modules silently overwrite. mcp_client.py has only an exact-name pin compare (refresh_tools:110 re-keys without any compare). No lookalike/confusable/edit-distance or normalization check exists: a name such as 'po.create' with a Cyrillic letter, or a trailing space, is just an unpinned new name at refresh and is accepted with no conflict flag. Name-comparison sites checked: mcp_client.py:95, tools/__init__.py:66, loop.py:59.

checks.check: Approval is bound to the verified server identity, so a new server with a matching tool name or self-reported name does not inherit approval or replace the approved tool.
checks.verify: 1) Find where tool approval is stored and checked. 2) Check approval is keyed by verified server identity, not tool name or self-reported server name. 3) Answer no if a new server with a matching tool name or server name would count as approved or replace the approved tool.
checks.note: Approvals are looked up by tool name, target and tenant only. No server identity is stored or compared, so a different server exposing the same tool name would inherit approval. refresh_tools (mcp_client.py:107-111) swaps the tool set with no pin check.

red_flags_found: app/mcp_client.py:110 refresh_tools replaces the whole tool map with no pin or name check (pins are only checked in initialize)
violates: Flag lookalike and duplicate names across servers
findings.summary: Tools are keyed by bare name, duplicates overwrite silently, and approval is not bound to a server identity.
findings.next_step: Key the registry and approvals by verified endpoint/registry namespace plus tool name, raise a conflict on duplicate or confusable names, and apply pin checks on refresh.

findings.title: Enforced gateway boundary
findings.requirement: Send MCP calls through a gateway or equivalent enforcement layer the agent cannot bypass. Choose controls for internal HTTP servers, public third-party services, and local stdio servers; private networking and mTLS are one internal deployment pattern, not universal MCP requirements. Authenticate each caller, preserve agent and delegated-subject identity, and authorize each action's tool, operation, resource, tenant, and arguments. Apply the same policy to direct calls, dynamic tools, CLI/code mode, and wrappers. Validate calls and responses, enforce rate limits, and log every decision. For HTTP OAuth, validate access tokens for the gateway's own audience, issuer, expiry, and scopes; obtain separately authorized backend credentials through a trusted issuer or supported exchange. Never accept a token for another resource or relay it unchanged as a substitute for backend authorization. Keep backend secrets and tokens away from agent-controlled execution paths. Restrict local process launch, files, environment, credentials, and network in the host or sandbox. Under MCP 2026-07-28, reject metadata-header/body mismatches before routing or policy relies on them. Isolate private caches by verified authorization context, tenant, resource, and policy version; share only data explicitly approved as public. Authorize explicit task/state handles on every operation; neither a connection nor self-reported metadata establishes identity. Where the gateway is an OAuth client, validate authorization-server issuer responses and protect discovery URLs against SSRF. Record protocol and extension versions and test each enabled extension's boundary, including task access/cancellation and MCP Apps sandbox, CSP, bridge messages, and UI-initiated tool authorization. Test bypass, cross-tenant access, malformed traffic, and required-check outages. Required checks fail closed.

not_covered.problem: Tool inventory missing a task-based reason for each tool
Agent credential granting wildcard or admin permissions
Destructive actions running without a higher-authority approval
Hidden instructions inside a tool's metadata
Outbound traffic to unapproved internet destinations

evidence.note: Backend token cache is keyed by audience/scope/tenant only, so a token minted for one delegated subject's run is reused for other users' runs in the tenant. The delegated subject is sent as a bare unverified string actor_token (identity.py:109). Gateway-side audience/issuer validation is outside this repo.

checks.check: Every governed tool path uses an enforced boundary suited to its internal HTTP, public third-party, or local stdio deployment; agent-controlled code cannot bypass it or obtain backend credentials.
checks.verify: 1) Inventory HTTP, dynamic, CLI/code-mode, wrapper and local-process paths. 2) Trace effective egress, backend credential custody and process/file/env/network restrictions. 3) Internal private networking/mTLS is one option; public services can use agent-side egress and broker-held credentials. 4) Reject any usable unmediated path; do not require operator control of a public provider's network. Use unknown for enforcement outside this repo.

checks.check: The gateway validates its own incoming token audience, issuer, expiry and scopes, and obtains separately authorized, backend-specific credentials while preserving agent and delegated-subject identity.

checks.verify: 1) Enumerate every execution path, not only tools/call. 2) Trace the same authorization, validation, quota and logging policy in each. 3) Reject alternate paths that invoke a disabled or denied tool, authorize only a tool name, or change tenant/resource authority. checks.check: Under MCP 2026-07-28, relevant header/body mismatches are rejected before routing or policy relies on them, and private caches/state/task handles are isolated by verified authorization context, tenant, resource and policy version.
checks.verify: 1) Identify supported protocol versions. 2) For 2026-07-28, trace version/method/name/parameter header validation before affected routing/policy decisions. 3) Trace cache keys/invalidation and every task/state-handle operation, including status/results and cancellation where present. 4) Reject cross-tenant/caller reads or stale grants after revocation; permit shared cache entries only when explicitly public. 5) Do not require removed protocol sessions for 2026-07-28; test legacy session binding only when that version is enabled.

checks.check: If the gateway is itself an OAuth client, it checks the authorization server's issuer (iss, RFC 9207) and blocks private and metadata addresses in discovery URLs. Answer yes with the code line, or yes citing the config that shows it isn't an OAuth client.
checks.verify: 1) Check whether the gateway acts as an OAuth client (gets tokens, follows discovery or metadata URLs). 2) If so, check RFC 9207 issuer-response comparison and rejection when an advertised required iss is missing; do not require an absent iss when the selected protocol permits it. Check it blocks unauthorized private, loopback, and metadata destinations, including on redirects and DNS resolution. Explicitly approved internal issuer endpoints may be allowed by trusted configuration; untrusted discovery must not widen that allowlist. 3) Answer no if either is missing. If it is not an OAuth client, answer yes citing the config that shows that.
checks.note: No OAuth discovery or metadata URL fetching in the repo; STS_URL is fixed config (settings.py). Whether the gateway is itself an OAuth client is outside this repo.

checks.check: Enabled MCP extensions have recorded versions and enforced boundaries, including Tasks ownership/cancellation and Apps sandbox/CSP/bridge/tool-call authorization where present.
checks.verify: 1) Inventory enabled extensions and versions from client/server/host configuration. 2) Trace extension-specific authorization, task ownership/status/results/cancellation, and Apps host sandbox, CSP, bridge-message validation and UI-triggered tool policy. 3) Reject a bypass or missing required boundary. 4) Answer yes for absent extensions only with configuration evidence; answer unknown for external host behavior not visible here.

findings.title: Untrusted peer messages
findings.requirement: Authenticate the sending agent (prove its identity) on every message, even validly signed ones. Validate message types and schemas, and check what that peer is allowed to ask for. Where a replay could repeat an action, check freshness and track nonces or request IDs. Checking the sender alone doesn't stop replays. Test faked identity, replayed requests, requests across tenants, and instructions passed along by a compromised peer. Verify signed agent cards where they exist. A card says who an agent is, not what it may do. Check callback and webhook URLs against SSRF. A valid sender doesn't make a message's content trusted.

not_covered.problem: Tool server identified only by its self-reported name
Missing schema or size checks on API responses
Peers or children still running after a stop
Run can't be rebuilt across gateway, tool services, and delegated workers

findings.title: Bounded delegated authority
findings.requirement: Give sub-agents only the powers approved for their task. Preserve the verified original subject and current actor through each handoff and enforce their task, tenant, resource, and audience limits where the action runs. Use supported token exchange or narrow task credentials rather than copying a parent's full credential. A parent must not gain a denied power by asking a more powerful peer to act without separate valid approval. For RFC 8693 tokens, earlier nested actors are provenance only and never add access. An actor chain or signed identity does not prove that a requested action was approved. Test legitimate delegation and that escalation attempt.

not_covered.problem: Approvals that can be replayed or aren't tied to exact arguments
Prompt a parent gave a sub-agent not recorded
Children still running after the parent is stopped
Replayed or faked peer-agent messages
No limit on how many sub-agents a run can start

evidence.note: child() copies the parent identity via replace() and only changes instance id and role. The child has no credential of its own: TokenBroker (identity.py:94-117) exchanges the same pod workload token and caches by (audience, scope, tenant), so parent and child share tokens. Also the child role is 'line_item_extractor' (extractor.py:25) but tools.yaml defines 'extractor' (tools.yaml:14), so build_registry falls back to the full procurement tool set (tools/__init__.py:69), including pay_invoice, erp_call and memory_write.

checks.check: Each child gets a credential narrowed to its approved task (for example by token exchange or transaction tokens), never the parent's full credential.
checks.verify: 1) Find where a child agent gets its credential. 2) Check it is a narrowed token for the task (token exchange, transaction token, scoped-down role). 3) Answer no if any spawn path passes the parent's token, API key, or full role, or the child inherits the parent's environment credentials.

Also the child role is 'line_item_extractor' (extractor.py:25) but tools.yaml defines 'extractor' (tools.yaml:14), so build_registry falls back to the full procurement tool set (tools/__init__.py:69), including pay_invoice, erp_call and memory_write.

checks.check: Authorization at the action uses the original subject and the current actor, and earlier actors in the delegation chain never add access.
checks.verify: 1) Open authorization code for delegated actions. 2) Check it decides on the original subject and the current actor. 3) Answer no if it grants access because of any earlier actor in the chain (nested `act` claims, parent identity) or a union of chain permissions.
checks.note: Token exchange sends the workload token as subject and the delegated subject as a bare actor_token string (identity.py:102-111); the child adds no further actor. The decision at each action is made by the STS/downstream services outside this repo. In-repo gate decisions (gate.py:32-47) do not look at parent identity.

checks.check: An action the parent was denied is also denied when routed through a more powerful peer, unless it carries its own explicit approval.
checks.verify: 1) Find how a parent asks a peer or child to act. 2) Check the request carries the parent's limits and the peer re-checks them, or requires its own explicit approval. 3) Answer no if a peer acts with its own wider permissions on a parent's request without that check.
checks.note: Child tool calls go through the same execute_tool and PolicyGate (extractor.py:96, loop.py:67), and the child has no wider credentials than the parent, so no more-powerful peer exists in the repo. Approvals are keyed by tool/target/tenant (approvals.py:76-86) not by instance, so the child can consume the parent's approvals; that binding belongs to B06.

checks.check: Downstream services reject the parent's token when the child presents it (audience-bound tokens).
checks.verify: 1) Find how child tokens are issued and how downstream services validate tokens. 2) Check tokens are audience-bound and services verify `aud`. 3) Answer no if audience is unset, a wildcard, or not checked. Answer unknown if downstream services are outside this repo.
checks.note: No child-specific token is issued: the child presents the identical cached token as the parent, so a downstream service cannot reject the parent's token when the child presents it. Audience is set (identity.py:106); downstream aud validation is outside this repo.

findings.next_step: Fix the role name so the extractor gets only read_document, and issue per-child narrowed tokens keyed by agent instance via token exchange.

findings.title: Recursive shutdown
findings.requirement: Run a drill across a parent, nested children, remote workers, queued work, and open tool streams, subscriptions, and tasks, where they exist. Check that the stop reaches every descendant within the set time. It must revoke access as needed and prevent orphaned retries or restarts. Record how outside effects that already happened are reconciled.

not_covered.problem: Agent able to disable or delay its own stop
No way to cut off the agent's access without cutting off the user
No drill for a compromised shared tool or agent type
Sub-agent given powers beyond its task

evidence.note: The halt flag is read once at run start. The model loop (loop.py:139) and the extractor loop (extractor.py:64) never re-check it, /runs launches runs as untracked tasks (main.py:159), and nothing sends a cancel to children, open requests or MCP tasks. A halt does not reach runs already in progress.

checks.check: A stop signal from the root reaches every descendant: nested children, remote workers, queued work, and open tool streams, subscriptions, and tasks.
checks.verify: 1) Find the stop handler. 2) Check it reaches nested children, remote workers, queued jobs, and open tool streams, subscriptions, and tasks (cancel calls, MCP `notifications/cancelled`). 3) Answer no if any of these that exists in the code is not reached, or stop only sets an in-process flag that remote workers never read.
checks.note: The halt flag is read once at run start. The model loop (loop.py:139) and the extractor loop (extractor.py:64) never re-check it, /runs launches runs as untracked tasks (main.py:159), and nothing sends a cancel to children, open requests or MCP tasks. A halt does not reach runs already in progress.

checks.check: Stopping revokes descendants' credentials or leases, and leases or tokens are short-lived, so a disconnected worker loses authority within the stop time limit.
checks.verify: 1) Open the stop path and credential issuing code. 2) Check stopping revokes descendants' tokens or leases. 3) Check token or lease lifetime fits within the stop time limit. 4) Answer no if no revocation exists, or tokens are long-lived so a disconnected worker keeps authority.
checks.note: Stop path performs no revocation of tokens or leases. Cached tokens stay in use until expiry and no revoke endpoint is called anywhere in app/. Lifetime is set by the STS (outside repo) and is not tied to a stop time limit.

checks.check: Queues and schedulers refuse new work, retries, and restarts for a stopped tree.
checks.verify: 1) Find queue consumers, schedulers, and retry logic. 2) Check each looks up the stopped state before running new work, retries, or restarts. 3) Answer no if any consumer, retry decorator, or restart policy runs without that check.
checks.note: Child spawn does not check stopped state. No queue exists, but spawn, tool calls and the background sweeper (main.py:68-77) run without a halt check; only new runs are refused (loop.py:127).

checks.check: Outside effects already completed are recorded for reconciliation.
checks.verify: 1) Open the stop path. 2) Check it records outside effects already completed (tool calls, writes, sent messages) for reconciliation. 3) Answer no if nothing is recorded, or only in-flight work is listed.
checks.note: The only stop code raises at run start. It records nothing about completed outside effects. Audit rows of tool_result exist (loop.py:95) but no stop-time reconciliation is produced.

violates: Check that the stop reaches every descendant within the set time
findings.summary: The halt flag is only read at run start, so running parents and children, in-flight tool calls and cached tokens are not stopped.
findings.next_step: Check halt state before every model turn, tool call and child spawn, track and cancel descendant tasks, revoke leases on stop and record effects completed before the stop.
